text:
jess: Heads-up — seeing tag interleaving / slot reuse weirdness in prod-rt KV cache after the compaction window. Two user streams ended up with shifted token alignment across requests. Dumped a few traces here: https://redwood.internal/gists/kv-dump-2147654321
perf-alert-bot: KV cache mem-spike detected on prod-rt-3 (p95 tokens +2.1x) at 2026-03-09T11:03:21Z :eyes:
omar: ugh, any repro steps? is this cross-request contamination or just stale blocks being replayed?
linh: initial read looks like slot metadata (tag) was overwritten during a concurrent compaction, then later requests read a compacted page with mixed request_ids. small repro with long-context chat + back-to-back requests reproduces ~20% of the time.
sam: can you paste the minimal repro? I can run locally with the KV page stress flag.
jess: minimal repro: two clients A/B, stream A writes a long context, then B issues short prompt while compaction runs. repro script attached: `scripts/repro/slot_interleave.sh`
jenkins-bot: deploy-prod-rt-3 completed at 2026-03-09T10:58:02Z (no restarts)
omar: example log snippet: `KV_PAGE_COMPACT slot=0x7f12 tag=0x3f req=abcd1234 -> write slot=0x7f12 tag=0x2a req=ef56` then later `KV_READ slot=0x7f12 tag=0x3f req=abcd1234` — tag mismatch + stale content
linh: also saw kernel-switch around the same time on that host (cuda kernel selector switched to int8 path) — might be correlated with timing that allows concurrent compaction to race with append.
maria: I ran the repro under tsan-ish config, got a fast-fail: `assert(slot->tag == expected_tag) failed` at kvpage.cc:412. Patch idea: fence compaction+append with sequence-epoch checks + bump refcounts during compaction.
infra-bot: perf-trace uploaded: https://redwood.internal/traces/2147654321/trace.json (look for thread 1024, compaction events 11:03:20-11:03:22)
sam: quick triage notes: 1) we have two problems mixed: stale reads (wrong tag) and alignment drift (token index shifted when KV prefetch assumes contiguous pages). 2) immediate mitigation: throttle compaction during high-Throughput streaming or disable async compaction on prod-rt hot nodes.
jess: agreed. can we do a canary patch that adds an assert/repair: on read detect tag mismatch -> drop page and force reload from backing store + emit telemetry? low-risk and will stop cross-request contamination.
linh: will open PR with double-check guards + metrics. I'll also add a short-term rollout that disables async compaction on the Dedicated tier during peak.
omar: also add a regression test in evict_suite that runs long-context streaming for 10k tokens and interleaves compaction ops. Add a fuzz case that flips kernel selection to force timing changes.
maria: queued heap profiles show leak only when stale blocks are reused across requests; new guard should stop reuse, so mem-growth should go back to baseline.
jess: thanks — assigning follow-ups: @linh PR, @omar test, @sam canary. If anyone sees recurrence after patch, ping here and paste kv dump. :thumbsup:
